title: fetch and ajax
summary: How a front end gets data from a server: what an HTTP request is, why requests are asynchronous, how promises stand in for data that hasn't arrived yet, and handling results with .then().catch().finally() or async/await. The curriculum uses Axios (a request library) and the PokeAPI; the browser's built-in fetch does the same job. The lesson also sets up a React + Vite project (with Docker). Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Request data from a public API, show it, and handle errors using both .then() and async/await.

steps.title: Read the Asynchronous Requests lesson
steps.detail: Read 'Asynchronous Requests' (and skim 'React and Vite', which covers the project setup). Focus on 'Breaking Down Promises' and 'Common Issues with Requests'.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain what a promise is in one sentence.

steps.title: Call the PokeAPI with fetch in Node
steps.detail: Node 26 has fetch built in. Save as poke.mjs and run node poke.mjs. Then change pikachu to a fake name: fetch does not throw on a 404, so you have to check res.ok yourself (Axios throws for you).
steps.doneWhen: It prints pikachu 25; the fake name prints the 404 error message.

steps.title: Rewrite it with .then().catch().finally()
steps.detail: The lesson teaches both styles. Rewrite the same request as a .then() chain so you can read either style.
steps.doneWhen: Both versions print the same output.

steps.title: Find the requests in Myflix
steps.detail: Myflix already talks to a server: supabase-js sends HTTP requests to Supabase for you. Open assignments/week-02/netflix/src/lib/librarySync.js and find the await calls, including the Promise.all that loads several tables at once.
steps.doneWhen: You can point to one await and say what data it is waiting for.

concepts.meaning: A message from the browser asking a server for data (GET) or sending it (POST).
Code that starts a task and keeps going instead of freezing while it waits.
A placeholder for a value that will arrive later, or an error if it fails.
Syntax that lets you wait for a promise in code that reads top to bottom.
A popular library for HTTP requests; it parses JSON and throws on error statuses for you.
